title: The Agent Works. Does Anyone Trust It? — Michele Grant, Leading at Scale
talk_summary: A governance/change-management talk about earning trust in enterprise AI agents via a value case, three-lines-of-defense ownership, and an autonomy scorecard.

takeaways.technique: Staged autonomy ladder with independent sampling
takeaways.what_they_do: Grant agent autonomy in four stages: shadow mode, supervised draft (review every line), exception ensemble (review flagged items plus random sample), then exceptions-only with periodic independent sampling to catch what the agent failed to flag.
takeaways.evidence_quote: once humans only look at exceptions, your biggest vulnerability is what the agent failed to flag

takeaways.technique: Override-rate and miss-rate as control metrics
takeaways.what_they_do: Track override rate and independently sampled missed material issues side by side with value metrics; a falling override rate may mean review depth slipped, not that the agent improved.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A falling override rate does not automatically mean the agent is getting smarter. It can also mean the depth of review has slipped.

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep core math/reconciliation rules in deterministic approved code; treat the model's written summary as explanation, not proof; real proof is telemetry of records pulled, tools run, and sign-off.
takeaways.evidence_quote: treat the model's written summary as a helpful explanation, not proof. Your real proof lives in the telemetry.

takeaways.what_they_do: For each item evaluated, record raw data ingested, tool calls, prompt, model version, output, and human sign-off, so autonomy decisions rest on evidence.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it records the raw data ingested, the tool calls executed, the prompt, and the mono versions. Output generated along with the human sign-off

takeaways.what_they_do: Maintain a model inventory record documenting regression triggers: any base-model or source-API update requires full revalidation before returning to production.
takeaways.evidence_quote: regression triggers, which are any updates to our current base model or source API that require full revalidation before running in production again

takeaways.what_they_do: Require a written value case with baselines (cycle time, hours returned, detection time) before an agent touches production; if you cannot state the baseline, do not deploy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If the IMO cannot state the baseline today, do not deploy. If you can't measure where you started, you can never prove the agent moved the needle.
takeaways.numbers: 80 analyst hours/week returned; report cycle 5 days to 2 days target
